segments.t: Kostya volunteers to bring the champagne to room 202 himself so he can film Louis and Polina together as proof for Nastya. Meanwhile, Senya and Fedya finish feeding their model for the third time and eagerly await their promised reward.

'Let me bring you the champagne myself.' The meaning hinges on 'come on' working together with 'champagne' in spoken Russian.

'You will bring it right to the room, that is great!' An emphatic spoken line centered on the verb meaning 'to bring'.

'Remember, we have room two hundred and two.' Louis brings out the contrast between 'to remember' and 'at' in a few short words.

'Thank you very much for your help, Kostya.' In Russian, the idea of 'very much' flows naturally into 'Kostya' without extra filler words.

'Sasha, watch my bar for now.' Notice how Russian expresses 'Sasha' and 'bar' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.

'Just mind you do not do like Louis!' Kostya anchors the line on 'only', while 'Louis' completes the thought.
Скажи, тебе было сегодня очень вкусно?
'Tell us, was it very tasty for you today?' The grammar packs 'say' and 'deliciously' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Молодцы, вы честно заслужили свою награду.
'Well done, you honestly earned your reward.' Senya anchors the line on 'well done', while 'reward' completes the thought.

'Well come on and reward us quickly already!' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'come on' before landing on 'us'.
Мы честно кормили тебя два дня.
'We honestly fed you for two days.' Senya anchors the line on 'we', while 'day' completes the thought.
Хорошо, ребята, закройте пока свои глаза.
'Alright, guys, close your eyes for now.' In Russian, the idea of 'well' flows naturally into 'eyes' without extra filler words. Senya answers right away.
